checks.covers: A zip archive extracted whole with no inspection of its entries in sight (no entry listing, so no size or entry-count check).
checks.misses: Tar archives (the rule accepts a filter, which checks paths and links, not sizes), a loop that inspects the entries for something other than their sizes, limits held in a wrapper or a library option, and decompressors that are not archives (gzip streams, office documents).

checks.covers: An archive extracted whole to a directory with no comparison of a length in sight.
checks.misses: Entry-by-entry extraction (the rule checks only the destination path there, never sizes or entry counts), a length compared against something other than the archive size, limits held in a wrapper or a library option, and decompressors that are not archives.

checks.covers: A zip archive extracted whole with no comparison of a length in sight.
checks.misses: Entry-by-entry extraction (the rule checks only the destination path there, never sizes or entry counts), a length compared against something other than the archive size, limits held in a wrapper or a library option, and decompressors that are not archives.

checks.covers: An archive unpacked whole, or an entry written out, with no read of an entry size or a size cap in sight.
checks.misses: The entry count is never looked at, a size read for another purpose silences the rule, limits held in a wrapper or a library option, and decompressors that are not archives.

checks.covers: A model reading of whether limits are checked after every expansion of an archive or compressed file.
checks.misses: It finds missing limits in the paths the model read and cannot show every archive path is bounded.

entries.why: Where an extraction call shows no sign of reading entry sizes (zip in Python, whole-archive calls in Java and C#, Rust), no size limit can have been applied before it; the rules for JavaScript, Go and PHP never look at sizes and are not tied to this requirement.

checks.covers: Uploads and stored files that accumulate without a per-user or aggregate limit, read by a model.
checks.misses: It finds missing quotas in the paths the model read and cannot see storage limits applied by the platform.

checks.covers: A reading of the project's source by a model against this requirement.
checks.misses: It reads the files the model was given and says only what it found there: behaviour at run time, code outside the scope and the parts of a flow the model did not read stay unexamined.

entries.why: An AI reading of the source for a per-user file count and size quota on stored uploads.

checks.covers: A tar archive extracted with no filter argument, the argument that carries the refusal of link entries in JavaScript.
checks.misses: A filter that does not refuse links, zip libraries (extraction through them is flagged for its missing path guard, not for links), archives rejected at upload by another component, and libraries the rule does not model. A silent result does not show links were refused.

checks.covers: A tar archive extracted with no filter argument, or with the fully_trusted filter, the argument that carries the refusal of link entries in Python.
checks.misses: A filter that does not refuse links (the tar filter or one the project wrote), zip archives, archives rejected at upload by another component, and libraries the rule does not model. A silent result does not show links were refused.

entries.why: Only the tar extraction calls of Python and JavaScript expose a filter argument that refuses link entries, so a call without one is the one place these rules can see links; the rules of the other languages look at paths only.

checks.covers: The image library's decompression-bomb pixel limit switched off.
checks.misses: A pixel limit of a very large value, images opened through other libraries, and a size check made before the image is opened.

entries.why: Switching the image library's pixel limit off is the configuration this requirement is about; the rule exists for Python's imaging library only.
